(D)uplicate (D)oses Heatmap

Source: R/dd_heatmap.R
dd_heatmap.Rd

Generates a heatmap of duplicate (or repeated) records from the output of dd_rate. The heatmap naturally combines two variables, so it can be used to visualize the data for each geographic area and one of the other disaggregation variables: vaccines or birth cohorts. data must therefore come from dd_rate with a geo_level of "ADM1" or "ADM2" and a value for disaggregate_by.

Usage

dd_heatmap(
  data,
  value = "rate",
  duplication = "duplicate",
  within_ADM1 = NULL,
  min_total = NULL,
  digits = 1,
  show_numbers = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

The output from the immunabc::dd_rate function.

value

Character. What to show in the cells: "rate" (default), the percentage of records in the duplication category, which shows where the problem is proportionally worst; or "n", the total number, which shows where most records need correcting.

duplication

Character. Which records to show: "duplicate" (default), the extra records with the same person, dose, vaccination date and place of occurrence as an earlier record; or "repeated", the extra records with the same person and dose but a different date or place.

within_ADM1

Character (optional). When analyzing data at the "ADM2" level, this optional character vector lets you specify one or several "ADM1" to filter. Default is NULL, which means no filtering by "ADM1".

min_total

Numeric (optional). Minimum number of records for a cell to be filled, since rates based on few records can be misleading. Other cells are grey and blank. Default is NULL, which fills all cells.

digits

The number of digits to show in the cells when value is "rate". Default is 1.

show_numbers

Logical. Whether to show the number in each cell (TRUE, default) or a color legend instead (FALSE). Use when there are too many cells to read their numbers (e.g. at the "ADM2" level).

Value

A ggplot object representing the heatmap.
